text: Lessons 7 through 9 protected data at rest, reduced casual exposure, and built a record of who touched what. All three quietly assumed something this lesson hasn't built yet: that Overlook's accounts only have the access they actually need.

A built-in role like db_datareader reads every table forever, including ones added next year. Named object-level grants read exactly the tables actually needed, and nothing else. For a healthcare database, that narrower choice is the one that matches the board's mandate.

The real pattern: create a custom role, grant it exactly the permissions it needs, and add the right account as a member. The scheduling app's role reads and writes appointments only. The reporting role reads patients and holds the unmask permission from Lesson 8 — the only role that sees real patient data, by design.

With encryption, masking, auditing, and least-privilege roles in place, Overlook's database is genuinely secured. Chapter 4 builds high availability and disaster recovery on top of exactly this now-secured foundation.
